chapter: Dizzy Gillespie, Yusef Lateef and 1960s New York
title: Yusef Lateef's world of scales and instruments
summary: Lateefian scales, shenai, oboe blues and flute effects widened Barron's ears.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: As long as we are bringing up the subject of versatility, you go back to Yusef. Yusef, to me, always had this huge conception. He seemed to embrace music influences and cultural experiences from everywhere.
So that is coming out in the music. How did that impact you? Or did it?
It did. It did, because it opened my ears to the same thing, the use of different kinds of scales that I would never have thought about using, what Ron Carter calls Lateefian scales.

Lateefian scales, and using other instruments. He used to play – he has this instrument called the shenai, an Indian instrument. Wow, oboe, playing blues on the oboe. Used to do See See Rider. He used to do that on oboe. So, yeah. Then sometimes he would make various sounds by – like he had played these wooden flutes, and he would make this sound by tapping the open end on his hand at the mic. Or sometimes he asked me to put my foot on the pedal, and he’d blow into the open – it would be like an echo. He was very much into that.
